transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49m (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Park (NimbusRetail Head of AI), Omar Aziz (Infra Lead), Priya Kapoor (PM)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is the usual weekly sync for the nimbus pilot, today we're focused on cost per unit — tokens per dollar and ops tradeoffs. diego will walk the bench results.
[00:18] Diego Ramos: hi all, quick caveat, couple of numbers are preliminary — there's some noise in the first run because prefix cache wasn't enabled for all shapes. i'll call out when i'm being rough. so baseline, hosted r-inference with rtx quantized 4bit variant: we're seeing about 950 tokens/sec at median for short prompts, cost roughly $0.0016 per 1k tokens — that aligns with earlier.
[00:43] Lena Park: can you repeat the tokens/sec per dollar metric, i missed the last part?
[00:48] Diego Ramos: sure. effectively with current batch=16 and no prefix cache, long-form prompts push latency up and reduce tokens/sec to ~420 which drives effective tokens/$ down to about 420k tokens per dollar — that is, fewer tokens. the exact dollar depends on whether you use hosted vs dedicated commit.
[01:12] Omar Aziz: is that on the 8k context model or 32k? because our calls will be 16k-20k typical.
[01:19] Diego Ramos: 16k context tests. the 32k runs we did had larger KV pressure so tokens/sec dropped further, about 300 tokens/sec for dense long convo with few-shot.
[01:35] Priya Kapoor: what's the biggest lever to improve tokens per dollar — batching or caching?
[01:40] Maya Chen: both, but they trade. batching improves compute efficiency but can hurt tail latency. caching — prefix or KV caching — can give big wins for repetition or system prompts. diego?
[01:49] Diego Ramos: yep. concrete numbers from today's run: enabling prefix cache for the 3 prompt archetypes gave a 28% median token/sec uplift for the long-form set. switching batch 16->8 reduced latency 30% but increased cost per token about 12% because less GPU utilization. so if your SLA needs <200ms tail, smaller batch. if throughput and cost matter, larger batch and async queueing.
[02:18] Lena Park: our product target is 250ms p95, most queries are mid-length 1-3k tokens. seems like batch=16 might be OK. but we need case-by-case.
[02:29] Omar Aziz: latency distribution matters — can you share the p95 numbers not just median?
[02:33] Diego Ramos: yes, p95 for batch16 with cache on for mid-length is 280ms; with batch8 it goes to 190ms. those numbers are on the hosted cluster.
[02:46] Priya Kapoor: what's the expected cost delta if we move to dedicated reserved capacity?
[02:51] Maya Chen: reserved typically drops unit infra cost by 25-40% depending on commit and instance type. Diego, you have a rough amortized per-token for the dedicated baseline?
[02:59] Diego Ramos: rough ballpark: for heavy-commit (reserved) we can get to ~600k tokens per dollar on mid-length workloads with cache and batch tuned, vs 420k without. but you lose flexibility and need commit sizes.
[03:17] Lena Park: there's also data residency and VPC — we may need private deployment for checkout flows. does that change numbers?
[03:24] Diego Ramos: private (VPC) adds a small infra overhead: network egress can add latency, and on-prem packaging can increase cost 10-20% because of ops. but privacy benefits may justify.
[03:37] Omar Aziz: SOC2 and KMS are must-haves — we saw in the security review that key rotation is important. Any blockers there?
[03:44] Maya Chen: we've shared SOC2 attestation and KMS integration docs in the drive. no blockers from our side; Diego, anything technical?
[03:50] Diego Ramos: KMS integration tested with customer-managed keys in the sandbox. audit logs need a slight config change but supported.
[03:57] Lena Park: good. back to cost — are there quick wins for cost beyond caching and batching? quantization?
[04:03] Diego Ramos: yes. 4-bit quantization is already applied in these runs; moving to mixed-int8 variants can give another 10-15% token/sec improvement in some models but sometimes harms output quality on certain prompts. we recommend running quality evals. also tokenization differences between models can change effective tokens per user request.
[04:24] Priya Kapoor: we have some hallucination concerns — any change in quantization could affect quality. we'll need regression tests.
[04:30] Diego Ramos: absolutely, quality gating is part of Redwood Optimize — you can tie regressions to eval prompts and auto-rollback.
[04:39] [05:00] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[05:05] Diego Ramos: i want to call out a weird artifact — in one run the prefix cache gave only 5% improvement for a specific prompt family because the prompts had dynamic session ids that prevented cache hits. so we'll need to canonicalize prompts before caching.
[05:22] Lena Park: that's our fault — some of our devs include trace ids in prompts. we'll scrub on our side.
[05:27] Maya Chen: ok action: priya to provide canonicalization rules and examples.
[05:33] Priya Kapoor: noted. we'll send a sample pipeline for prompt normalization.
[05:36] Diego Ramos: on batching tradeoffs — one idea is dynamic batching by priority: small interactive queries go low latency path (batch=4) and background tasks batch to higher sizes. Redwood's routing can do policy-based routing by route.
[05:51] Omar Aziz: that would help. do you have a config example?
[05:55] Diego Ramos: yes, i'll drop a sample routing policy in the drive.
[05:58] Maya Chen: also, Diego will run a 1-hour synthetic benchmark that mirrors Priya's 95th percentile traffic shape to validate tokens/sec/$ across batch sizes 8/16/32 with cache on/off.
[06:13] Lena Park: good. on pricing, can you show breakouts per route? we want to know if checkout flows cost more.
[06:19] Maya Chen: we'll add per-route estimates in the pricing sheet — Diego will produce per-route tokens/sec and Maya will map to dollars with the pilot discount.
[06:28] Priya Kapoor: on the subject of fallbacks — if we hit capacity, what's the automatic fallback story?
[06:33] Diego Ramos: Redwood can route to a cheaper model variant (smaller or lower context) or to a cross-region fallback. you can define predicates: latency breach => fallback to xo-model-compact, etc. quality guardrails possible.
[06:48] Lena Park: curious, did you run any benchmarking against Anthropic or OpenAI? i know the team is comparing per-token unit economics.
[06:55] Diego Ramos: we did some public benchmark comparisons; OpenAI has strong latency on their infra but pricing different; Anthropic models often have higher token counts for same utterance. those comparisons are noisy — we'll share the spreadsheet but note differences in tokenization and model family.
[07:12] Omar Aziz: anything in the benchmark about warm vs cold KV cache? how important is steady-state?
[07:18] Diego Ramos: warm cache matters a lot. first few requests have KV warmup cost. for steady-state with repeated users, caching contributed up to 40% reduction in per-token compute on our long form set.
[07:31] Priya Kapoor: let's document expected warmup window and how many users before steady-state.
[07:36] Diego Ramos: will do — i'll include a warmup model in the benchmark output.
[07:39] Lena Park: are there recommended observability metrics for us to track during pilot?
[07:44] Maya Chen: yes: tokens/sec, per-route cost, p50/p95 latency, cache hit rate, batch size distribution, kv cache size, and quality regression counts. we'll add token-level cost breakdowns.
[07:59] Omar Aziz: on security again, for private deployment do you push images into our registry or do we pull?
[08:05] Diego Ramos: we support both patterns. preferred is customer-pull with signed manifest, less surface area.
[08:11] Priya Kapoor: okay. next steps recap?
[08:14] Maya Chen: recap: diego run benchmarks (batch 8/16/32, cache on/off, warmup model) by 12/16; maya share updated pricing by 12/13; priya upload prompts and histogram by 12/15; schedule sizing call after bench.
[08:27] Lena Park: sounds good. also please call out which knobs materially change hallucination rates.
[08:33] Diego Ramos: will include quality checks per variant and quantization level.
[08:37] Priya Kapoor: one last thing — can you include an example JSON line for the routing policy so our infra team can vet it?
[08:43] Diego Ramos: yes, i will add an example policy doc.
[08:46] Maya Chen: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the drive.
[08:49] Lena Park: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
